output.summary: Approved G1039 design revision 3 (review round 2 approved, all prior findings resolved). In merge mode (G1038), a clean trunk sync keeps a node's checkpoint when its -U0 patch id is unchanged and every hand-resolved path in its scope equals `git merge-file --union` of the three versions; design and tests reviews then stay current. run_tests always re-runs; review_impl re-runs via a new base input with a shrinkable sync card section. The budget becomes a per-stage limit (default 10) on review rounds that raise new material findings, gated by capability round_budget; only review/op re-runs after a clean sync are exempt. Notes for implement: skip the union check when old and new checkpoint commits are equal; exclude `detail` from the fold condition; update render.py res.budget readers and test that next offers no delivery agent actions while discovery remains.

responses.review_design:1:1: fixed: §3.1/§3.2 add check 2. For each hand-resolved path inside the node's scope (every path when scope is None), M's blob must equal `git merge-file -p --union` of the W/B0/O versions, in either side order. Otherwise the node stales. The hand-resolved set is derived inside `unchanged()`, which keeps G1038's signature: `carry.resolved_paths(ident, M)` diffs M against G1038's merge-tree T, recomputed and memoized per M, and this equals synced.resolved. `carry.union_kept` does the comparison. The HISTORY both-rows case still carries in either order (verified). Interleaved, moved, wrong-copy, mixed-order and modify/delete resolutions stale the node. Tests 1 and 6 add the reordered and moved-line cases, and the moved-line test asserts that check 1 alone would have carried it. §1 now says 'trunk edits to the goal's own -/+ lines' and that context edits inside the -U3 hunk carry (test 4).
responses.review_design:1:2: fixed: §3.4 and the §4 table add `("blob", "sync", "touching")` to the size-sorted blob steps, keeping more and all. They also add `("fold", "sync")`, which runs after every blob step and folds everything except from/to/diff/log into one blob view, `sync.detail`. Both go into card._steps/_apply and the SPEC §4.20 list. The constant ask moves into review.md as an 'After a trunk sync' section. Prompts are not fingerprinted (SPEC §4.8), and the card has no `ask` key. Test 11 is restated: real re-run cards already exceed 4,096 bytes because `previous` is unshrunk (G1019's job). After shrink, `sync` is exactly {from, to, diff, log, detail}, so it adds at most one view. The previous-driven fixed point still holds.
responses.review_design:1:3: fixed: §3.5 exempts a record only when the node has no checkpoint outputs (`graph.checkpoint_outputs(n) == []`) and every stale key is a base-selecting input. In practice that is a review_impl re-run whose subject was carried. A test_design or implement re-run after a sync that carry refused counts when it raises a new material finding. Test 7 adds these rows: implement stale only on inputs.base with a new material finding -> 1; test_design the same -> 1; implement with no new finding -> 0. Also fixed the noted inconsistency: §3.5 and §4 now both call `res.budget` a shape change, not an additive one (used/agents/over are replaced by stages while round_budget is required, and the old shape is kept otherwise), and they list its in-repo readers.

output.summary: Revision 3 builds on revision 2 and fixes only the three round-1 findings. The carry predicate now needs two things: equal -U0 patch ids, and, for every hand-resolved path inside the node's scope, a merged blob equal to `git merge-file --union` of the three versions in either side order. The resolved paths are derived from the sync merge, so the HISTORY both-rows case still carries, and reordered, moved or wrong-copy resolutions stale the node. The card's `sync` section gets two shrink steps in card._steps and SPEC §4.20, and its constant ask text moves into review.md. Test 11 now bounds only what `sync` adds after shrink (one view), because `previous` keeps re-run cards over 4 KB (G1019). The budget exemption is limited to nodes with no checkpoint outputs, and `res.budget` is documented as a shape change.

responses.run_tests:failed: fixed: Reproduced the four failures and distinguished two real 4136-byte card regressions from two superseded legacy fixture assumptions. Named short instructions may now become full blob/read references without previews only after prior strategies exhaust and only when actual size shrinks; unavailable/non-storing readers retain inline text. Actual two cards measure4028 bytes with exact raw Git readback of complete guidance and unchanged base/scope/cost/checks fields. Four original IDs plus two tiny controls passed6 tests/15.605s; 74 shrink/property/prompt/docs controls passed/.353s; all six required commands passed91 tests. Shipped definition includes the approved base tuple; only the isolated G1022 fixture opts out, keeping original counter assertions. Budget/caller source is byte-identical to23428191, frozen7 unchanged, and independent delta review cleared.

output.summary: Fixed the two sync-review card-size regressions with a final lossless short-instruction reference fallback after existing compaction, retaining complete readable guidance and all base/scope/cost evidence. Updated the exact shipped-definition expectation for the approved base input and isolated the original G1022 definition-only migration from that later semantic edge, preserving its original stale-state and counter assertions. All four original failures, 74 related controls and six required commands pass; independent review cleared the delta, while all seven frozen files and budget/caller source remain unchanged.

findings.text: Clean-sync predicate: the -U0 patch id ignores position. With identity.py's DIFF flags at --unified=0 and patch-id --verbatim, the same goal line inserted after line 10 and after line 30 gives an identical id (1b4a7646dfe2 both times; the -U3 ids differ). §3.1 leaves synced.resolved out of the predicate and claims that equal -U0 ids mean 'exactly new trunk plus the goal's own lines'. That is false for hand-resolved files: keeping both sides in a different order, moving the goal's lines elsewhere in the file, or deleting the wrong copy of a duplicated line all keep the id. test_design is then carried and review_tests is skipped although the tests' meaning changed, which contradicts the spec ('conflict resolutions ... stale as today'). A trunk-only merge cannot move goal lines, so the gap is limited to synced.resolved. Fix: for each path in synced.resolved inside the node's scope, also require a position-aware check, for example that the resolved blob equals `git merge-file -p --union` of the B0/onto/tip versions in either side order (this still carries the HISTORY both-rows case); otherwise the node stales. Add tests for a reordered both-sides code resolution and for a moved goal line. Also align §1 ('trunk edits inside the goal's hunks' stale) with test 4, which carries context edits inside the -U3 hunk: say 'trunk edits to the goal's own -/+ lines'.

Sync card size: §3.4 says that over 4,096 bytes 'G1018's shrink steps blob sync.touching', but at f4eaf74 card._steps (and the SPEC §4.20 list) only blobs prompt, instructions, inputs/context/policy, corrections, candidates and notes, so a new top-level `sync` key is never shrunk. Real review_impl re-run cards are already at or over the target because `previous` is never shrunk (G1022 review_impl attempt 2 is about 4.0 KB, G1027 review_impl attempt 2 about 5.6 KB). Adding about 1.3 KB of inline sync, including a roughly 550-byte constant ask, makes about 7 KB. Test 11 ('at most 4,096 bytes after shrink, at real sizes') cannot hold, and it conflicts with test_a_card_over_budget_because_of_previous_is_a_fixed_point. Fix: specify new shrink steps in SPEC §4.20 and card.py (blob sync.touching, keeping more/all, then the rest of sync except from/to/diff/log) and list them in the §4 table. Consider moving the constant ask into review_impl's prompt or a fixed blob. Restate test 11 as a bound on what sync adds after shrink, plus the fixed point for a card over the target because of previous.

Budget exemption is too broad: §3.5 exempts any record that started stale with all of its stale keys being inputs selecting a git.base node, and calls this 'exactly the clean-sync review_impl re-run'. But test_design and implement also take base.base_commit as a non-context input. When carry rejects them (the sync was not clean for them), they re-run stale only on inputs.base and are exempt. They do raise new material findings (G1027 implement:1:1, G1026 test_design:1:1), and such a round is not caused by a clean sync. Fix: also require that the node has no checkpoint outputs (a checkpointing node stale only on base is one that carry refused), so in practice only review nodes whose subject was carried are exempt. Add a counts() row: implement stale only on inputs.base after a refused carry, raising a new material finding, counts 1.

output.summary: Revision 3 resolves all three round-1 findings. The union check on hand-resolved paths can only make carry stricter: byte-equal to a --union output or the node stales, and conflicts left at T's content are caught by check 1. It is evaluated once per sync with no loop. The shrink steps match card._steps/_apply at f4eaf74, and the budget exemption is keyed on checkpoint outputs. Three non-blocking notes for implement: a guard for the contained case, the fold condition excluding `detail`, and two more `res.budget.get("over")` readers in render.py (534, 562).

Approved: scoped transient U0 carry with conservative positional unions, truthful sync evidence and gated per-stage material-round budgeting match the design. Card guidance and legacy behavior are preserved; zero-budget empty-stage crash fixed; seven frozen files and default POLICY unchanged. Final tree37acf87b matches all7commands PASS and1090/1090 canonical tests in131.014s. No open findings; fresh CI pending.

A code-name/shared-file-only implementation can pass while missing acceptance 1: trunk adds .agents/fixtures/graph26/POLICY.json containing the plain JSON line "min": "0.0.0" that the goal removes from a different templates/default/POLICY.json. Extend the existing small Git/card fixture (or one equally small case) with those distinct paths, ensure graph26 is outside the shared changed-file intersection, and assert its touching entry explicitly identifies the added line the goal removes. Keep existing hand-resolution ordering/cap/shrink checks; no full journey or broad suite is needed.

spec:
Found while dogfooding Release 1. Every sync of a goal with the integration branch marks test_design, review_tests, implement, run_tests and review_impl stale, even when the goal's own diff did not change. G1027 synced twice and ran out of its correction budget (19 of 18) mostly that way.

Owner decisions (verbatim):
- "Ok I guess, but syncing to trunk changes things semantically like you said."
- On what re-runs after a sync merge where the goal's own diff didn't change, the owner chose "Tests + code review": design and tests reviews stay valid; run_tests always re-runs, and review_impl re-runs with a card focused on what the trunk merge brought in.
- "I think we may as well get these done now, before dogfooding again"

Scope:
- A sync whose goal diff is unchanged (the goal's own changes against the new trunk equal its changes against the old trunk, apart from context) keeps design, review_design, approve_design, test_design, review_tests and implement current.
- run_tests always re-runs after a sync.
- review_impl re-runs after a sync; its card shows what the trunk brought in that touches the goal (files the goal also changes, names it uses) and asks for semantic conflicts, not a full re-review.
- A sync that changes the goal's diff (conflict resolutions, or trunk changes inside the goal's hunks) stales as today.
- Re-runs caused by a clean sync do not count against the goal's correction budget.

Budget redefinition (owner: "Ok go with the recommendation", answering "why does a goal even _need_ a correction budget?"):
- The budget's job is to catch reviews that never converge (a new material finding every round, so no single finding repeats and no dispute fires). Today it counts every correction run, and its only firing in the Release 1 run (G1027, 19 of 18) was a false positive caused by syncs and reorder resubmits.
- Redefine it as a limit on review rounds per stage that raise new material findings. Re-runs after a clean sync, resubmits that only carry findings forward, and run_tests reruns do not count.
- Default about 10 such rounds per stage (G1026's design took 7 to 8 real rounds). Reaching it asks the owner, as today, to continue, hold or cancel.
- Acceptance adds: replaying G1027 does not reach the budget; replaying G1026's design rounds counts only rounds with new material findings.

Acceptance:
- Replaying G1027's second sync (onto G1022) keeps the reviews of design and tests, re-runs run_tests, and gives review_impl a sync-focused card that names the graph26 fixture change.
- A conflicting sync stales as today.
- This PR edits docs/design/SPEC.md and DESIGN.md for every contract change it makes and adds a HISTORY §4 row.
title: A clean trunk sync keeps design and tests reviews; run_tests and a focused code review re-run
